messages.subject: Re: Problem with simdata() from existing mirt model (Parameter Stability with Different Sample Sizes)
parts:
Information measures can only be interpreted when the data are the same across models. What you're doing here is comparing completely different datasets and trying to compare the magnitude of AIC and others, which doesn't make sense given how these measures are defined (they're effectively rescaled versions of the log-likelihood, which changes as a function of the available data). 

Phil


On Wed, Nov 15, 2023 at 8:47 AM Vince Star <vins...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello everyone,

I am currently working on an IRT simulation study using the 'mirt' package, where I treat model parameters from an initial fitted model as the true parameters to generate new datasets. My goal is to compare the stability of estimated model parameters against the "true" parameters with varying sample sizes. However, my results are somewhat counterintuitive, and I would like some guidance to understand if there is a conceptual error in my approach.

Below is a reproducible R example that illustrates my workflow:

library(mirt) # Fitting an initial model with the 'Science' dataset test <- mirt(Science, 1) # Simulating data with N = 2000 based on the initial model testsim2000 <- simdata(model=test, N=2000) # Fitting a new model on the simulated data test2 <- mirt(testsim2000, 1) # Comparing the initial and new model fits anova(test, test2)
            AIC     SABIC        HQ       BIC    logLik         X2 df   p
test   3249.739  3262.512  3274.922  3313.279 -1608.870                  
test2 16342.614 16381.395 16375.518 16432.228 -8155.307 -13092.875  0 NaN

The comparison of AIC, BIC, and log-likelihood suggests a major difference between 'test' and 'test2', indicating instability in parameters with an increased N.

However, when I simulate data with N equal to the original dataset size (N = 392):

# Simulating data with N = 392 based on the initial model testsim2000 <- simdata(model=test, N=392) # Fitting a new model on the new simulated data test2 <- mirt(testsim2000, 1) # Comparing the initial and new model fits anova(test, test2)
           AIC    SABIC       HQ      BIC    logLik      X2 df   p
test  3249.739 3262.512 3274.922 3313.279 -1608.870              
test2 3260.744 3273.517 3285.927 3324.285 -1614.372 -11.005  0 NaN

I find the estimated parameters to be more similar to the initial model, as expected. However, it seems paradoxical that increasing N does not get me closer to the true parameters but instead seems to lead to greater divergence.

I also noticed this with my data but  

My questions for the group are:

  1. Is there a theoretical explanation for why parameter estimates might diverge more with larger N in a simulation context?
  2. Do the AIC, SABIC,HQ,BIC and logLik comparisons make sense in this simulation framework or should I be considering different methods for evaluating parameter recovery/stability?

Thank you for your time.

Best regards,
